newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rabobank sees considerable profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Rabobank sees considerable profit rise.

text.p: UTRECHT, Netherlands, Feb 26 - Dutch cooperative Rabobank Nederland BA said on Wednesday it expected a considerable profit rise in 1997.
"It is too early to give a proper forecast ... but we expect a considerable profit increase should be possible (in 1997)," chairman Herman Wijffels told a news conference on the bank's 1996 results.
Wijffels said Rabobank's activities showed an average volume increase of about eight percent in recent years and said another major growth in volume terms was expected in 1997.
Profit growth should be in line with the increase in volumes, he added.

Earlier, Rabobank said its 1996 net profit had grown by 14 percent to 1.63 billion guilders. The unlisted bank's total lending rose by 14.1 percent to 220.8 billion guilders and interest income increased by 10.8 percent to 7.08 billion.
Rabobank's 1996 fee income increased by 16.9 percent to 1.25 billion guilders.
